title: Google Quantum AI Launches $150K Kaggle Competition to Compress Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits Using AI Agents - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Google Quantum AI launched a $150,000 Kaggle competition (October 22, 2026 to January 20, 2027) for compressing fault-tolerant quantum algorithm subroutines in fusion energy, optimization (DQI) and quantum chemistry (FeMoCo). It rests on kickmix, an open-source verification library in Qualtran that fuzz-tests circuits with tens of millions of gates classically, giving AI coding agents an automated reward signal.

insights.claim: Google Quantum AI launched a global Kaggle competition with a $150,000 prize pool for competitive programmers, AI researchers and circuit architects to compress critical subroutines in fault-tolerant quantum algorithms, running from October 22, 2026 to a January 20, 2027 deadline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Crowdsourcing circuit compression could further cut fault-tolerant resource estimates, pulling forward useful-quantum timelines.

insights.claim: The competition has three benchmarks: fixed-point 1/sqrt(x) phasing for plasma stopping power in inertial confinement fusion, a reversible Reed-Solomon syndrome decoder for Decoded Quantum Interferometry optimization, and tensor factorization/QROM co-optimization for the nitrogenase FeMoCo electronic structure.

insights.so_what: Shows Google's priority application targets for fault-tolerant machines: fusion energy, optimization and chemistry.

insights.claim: Kickmix is a new open-source C++20 and Python verification library in Google's Qualtran framework that lets classical CPUs fuzz-test candidate circuits with tens of millions of gates at up to 60 billion instructions per second on a single core.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cheap classical verification removes a key barrier to automated quantum circuit optimization.
insights.quote: fuzz-test candidate circuits with tens of millions of gates at rates up to 60 billion instructions per second on a single core
insights.locator: Detailed in a research preprint published

insights.claim: Although simulating arbitrary quantum circuits becomes intractable above roughly 40 qubits, the subroutines dominating fault-tolerant algorithm cost are built from kickmix circuits (reversible classical logic, diagonal phase gates and measurement-based uncomputation) that map basis states to basis states, so they can be fuzz-tested classically in linear time.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Most fault-tolerant cost sits in classically verifiable arithmetic, so classical tooling can drive major resource savings.

insights.claim: By combining SIMD bit-packing with the Fiat-Shamir heuristic, which seeds test inputs with a salted SHA-256 digest of the candidate circuit, the kickmix verifier gives AI coding agents and heuristic optimizers an automated, non-interactive reward signal to find bit-twiddling hacks without compromising accuracy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A verifiable reward signal is exactly what agentic AI needs, making quantum compilation a new RL/agent benchmark domain.
